context: Predicted baseline failure: with nothing in the fixture hinting at consolidation, the unaided agent authors one request per market - five written out and a note to repeat the pattern - or invents a parameterisation the tool cannot execute: a JavaScript array of markets inside a pre-request script looped with `pm.sendRequest`, the list stored as a collection variable, or a shell `for` loop invoking the runner once per row. All three produce something that reads like a covered matrix. The first two never exercise the request under test as a reported request; the third turns a single five-minute step into forty process launches. The runner's own iteration-data mechanism - one external CSV or JSON file fed in at run time, one pass per row through the same request - is the thing the agent is not expected to reach for.

checklist.name: Markets fed in as an iteration data file
checklist.description: The market list is a standalone CSV or JSON file passed to the run with the iteration-data flag (`-d` / `--iteration-data`), in the shape that flag consumes: a CSV whose header row names the variables, or a JSON array of flat objects. Scores zero if the list lives inside the collection (collection variables, a script-level array, one item per market) or if a data file is authored but never wired into the command. Scores at most half if the file's shape cannot be iterated row-per-pass (nested objects, a wrapper key around the array, a markdown table left as-is).

checklist.name: MUST NOT author one request per market
checklist.description: The delivered collection contains exactly one price request. Scores zero if it holds one item per country, or five items plus an instruction to duplicate for the remaining 35 - a 40-item collection is precisely the review burden finance asked to avoid, and it puts their list back behind an engineering change.

checklist.name: Request and checks read the current row
checklist.description: The request body substitutes the row's country (`{{country}}` or equivalent) and the checks compare the response against that row's expected currency and tax treatment, read through `pm.iterationData.get(...)` or equivalent substitution. Scores zero if the expected currency or tax flag is hard-coded to one market's value: the suite then passes all 40 passes while only ever proving one, and the report is green either way. Parameterising the body but not the expectations scores at most half.

checklist.name: One invocation covers every market
checklist.description: The delivered command is a single run of the collection with the data file attached. A shell loop calling the runner per row, a CI matrix per country, or forty steps score zero - the task rules each out explicitly and the budget is one step.

checklist.name: A failing market is named in the report
checklist.description: Check names or assertion messages interpolate the row's country so the report identifies the market that broke. All passes reporting under identical static names scores at most half - correct, but triage still means reading the raw log, which the task calls out. Scores zero if the design cannot distinguish markets at all, for example a single aggregate check over the whole run.

checklist.name: House conventions followed
checklist.description: The host comes from `{{baseUrl}}` and the key from `{{apiKey}}` via the `x-api-key` header, matching the orders collection, and the run passes the staging environment file with `-e`. A literal hostname or a literal key anywhere in the new collection scores zero.

checklist.name: Delivered collection is a valid v2.1 document
checklist.description: Parses as JSON with the v2.1 `info.schema` value, an `item` array, a structured `request.url`, and the test script attached as an `event` entry whose `script.exec` is an array of lines - the same shape as the orders collection. A hand-invented JSON shape, or a script stored as a single string where the house file uses a line array, scores at most half. No collection file delivered scores zero.

checklist.name: Orders collection untouched
checklist.description: `collections/orders.postman_collection.json` is unmodified. Editing it, or folding pricing requests into it, scores zero.
